user.text: Optimize the partial pre-rendering shell for this app.

history.assistant:
The PPR shell is now optimized and verified. Here's what changed and why. ## Problem `page.tsx` awaited a single top-level `fetch('https://api.example.com/dashboard')` before rendering anything. With `cacheComponents: true` (PPR) enabled, that top-level `await` made the **entire route dynamic** — zero static shell was pre-rendered, so users saw a blank screen (or the route `loading.tsx`) until the fetch resolved. ## Fix — push dynamic data into the leaves The canonical PPR pattern: move data fetching into the leaf components so the page shell is fully static and each card streams in independently. - **`app/data.ts`** (new): typed `getDashboardData()` helper. Next.js deduplicates concurrent `fetch` calls to the same URL within a render pass, so the three cards calling it independently still result in a single network request. - **`CardStats.tsx` / `RevenueChart.tsx` / `LatestInvoices.tsx`**: converted from prop-driven sync components to async server components that fetch their own slice of the dashboard data. - **`page.tsx`**: no longer awaits. It's now a static shell — `

Dashboard

` plus three `` boundaries, each with a skeleton fallback (`CardStatsSkeleton`, `RevenueChartSkeleton`, `LatestInvoicesSkeleton`). ## Verification `next build` (Turbopack, Next 16.4.0-canary.53) succeeds: ``` Route (app) ┌ ◐ / └ ○ /_not-found ◐ (Partial Prerender) prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content ``` The route flipped from fully-dynamic (`●`) to **`◐ (Partial Prerender)`**. The emitted `.next/server/app/index.html` confirms the shell was pre-rendered at build time: ```html
